rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Checked every pronoun/demonstrative/named-referent across all 4 chunks under a sequential read. Chunk 1 line 5 "You stepped away with the agent working" / "The session finished...": no prior in-file naming, but this file's maintainer Delivery-mode note pins it as an in-room M5 opener delivered directly after the M4 un-packaged send-off (verified against the host module: `learn-from-the-test.md:36` includes this file, and `learn-from-the-test.md:8` "Walk in with your un-packaged session" / :22 "You sent off an un-packaged session" already name the referent in the module's own signposting before this lecture is reached) -- clears both the module-arc-beats-in-openers/closers carve-out and the module-include-order carve-out. Chunk 2 line 11 "the same three" resolves against the chunk's own header ("Three failure modes..."), which counts as in-chunk per the rule. Chunk 2 line 15 "that window" resolves against "the window"/"the working window" named twice earlier in the SAME chunk (lines 12, 13). Chunk 3 line 19 "The un-packaged send-off was the test" -- same module-signposting carve-out as above, cross-checked live: `run-the-first-experiment.md:23,49` and `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/set-the-markers-send-it-off.md` (via grep) confirm "un-packaged send-off" is a currently-alive M4 beat, not stranded. Chunk 3 line 18 "This module holds that reflex off" -- "module" is never named earlier in-file, but this reads as a self-locating deictic (like "this document"/"this course") resolvable from the reader's own situation rather than requiring prior in-text naming; confirmed it is not a positional cross-file callback by checking the file's own module-free convention, defined in this file's accept-notes as "zero `M[0-9]` above the fence" (grep -noE 'M[0-9]' over body -> 0 hits, exit 1) -- the generic word "module" without a number is what that convention permits, so the reference is portable to whichever module includes the file, not broken by position.

grep -inE 'the opening lecture|earlier lecture|the previous (module|lecture|exercise)|prework at the top' over body lines 1-20 -> 0 hits. Closest candidate: chunk 3 line 19, "The un-packaged send-off was the test" -- names a real prior activity by role/title, not by page position (never "above", "in the last module", "three slides back"), clearing the navigational-pointer carve-out (name it, don't locate it). No sentence anywhere points at another file by relative position.

rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE "the .*(you (did|saw|caught|found|ran|sent))" over body lines 1-20 -> 0 hits: no literal "the X you did" construction. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: grep -inE 'guess|predict' over body lines 1-20 -> 0 hits (command run, no output, exit 1). No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in body; the file has no live-demo beat for this rule to check.

Chunk 0 is title-only (H1, no lede) -- the template's designated title-slide shape, not a wait-state fragment. Chunk 1 carries 3 multi-clause bullets each with its own claim (the artefact framing, the closing-summary warning, the driving question). Chunk 2 carries 5 bullets, three of them the named failure-mode handles. Chunk 3 carries 2 bullets (the reflex-off principle, the test->learn->encode mapping). None is a single context-dependent fragment of the kind the rule bans.

Chunk 1 header "What would have caught this earlier?", lines 3-8: closest candidate to a mismatch, since the chunk poses the question (bullet 3 restates it verbatim) rather than answering it -- but the header is the file's own stated diagnostic device, not a promise of an answer inside this chunk (backing block's `driving-question` claim: "the file's whole reason to exist, and deliberately a question rather than a checklist"), so the chunk's content (raw material for asking the question) matches what the header names. Chunk 2 header "Three failure modes you'll use to read", lines 9-15: content delivers exactly three named modes plus a related aside on rules files; header holds. Chunk 3 header "Diagnose first, fix later", lines 16-20: bullet 1 delivers "diagnose [first]" (holding the fix reflex off), bullet 2's "encode" step is the deferred "fix later"; header is not contradicted by either bullet.

Closest candidate: chunk 1 line 7, "Not *did the task succeed*. Not *should I have spec'd it tighter*." -- this is the reverse of the banned shape (banned = "Not X. Not Y. Z.", ending on an affirmed Z; here the affirmed clause [the driving question] comes FIRST and nothing follows the two negations), and it is a pair, not a triple, which the epistrophe sub-item explicitly allows ("cut to a pair" is the rule's own acceptable resolution for a would-be triple). The maintainer's 2026-08-25 accept-note confirms a THIRD sentence that used to follow this pair ("A diagnostic: you read the artefact...") was cut for restating its neighbour, leaving the pair alone with no trailing Z -- so the passage is now further from the banned shape than before, not closer. grep -inE 'one of the most|most useful|particularly (useful|valuable)' over body -> 0 hits (self-grading superlatives). No anaphora/epistrophe triples anywhere. No number-plus-retraction (the file states no numbers at all in body). No abstraction-noun stacks ("the working window", "the next likely word" are the file's own defined mechanism terms, not vague stacks). No empty-leg verb triplets.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate: chunk 3 header "Diagnose first, fix later", line 16 -- grammatically verb-initial (imperative-shaped), the mood the rule reserves for EXERCISE headers, not lecture headers. Reads inside as a durable maxim rather than a literal instruction to the reader, however: it is the closer of a merged file (`learning-through-contrast.md` per the 2026-08-25 accept-note) explicitly attested in this file's own backing block as a `vision`-class claim (`diagnose-first-fix-later`) naming the module's design philosophy, and it functions as "the beat where the file stops instructing and names a law that outlives the task" (per the rule's own description of what a declarative closer does) even though phrased as a two-verb aphorism rather than a subject-predicate sentence -- same register as a proverb ("Look before you leap"). Chunk 2 header "Three failure modes you'll use to read" is a catalogue entry naming its subject, an explicit NOT-violation shape. Chunk 1 header "What would have caught this earlier?" is the file's own driving diagnostic question, attested by the backing block's `driving-question` entry as deliberate; rewriting it into a flat claim would degrade the file's own stated design rather than merely restyle a heading.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Chunk 3 "Diagnose first, fix later", line 18: "This module holds that reflex off." -- class (b), self-referential design commentary: the sentence tells the student they are inside a deliberate pedagogical withholding, the same shape as the compendium's own cited example ("un-packaged first is by design"). The bullet's real payload survives without it: "the reflex is to fix it immediately... The failures earn the validation that catches them" already states the practice and its reason; the middle sentence adds only the meta-frame that the module was built this way on purpose, which is check_student_facing §33 territory (slides-class face, per this compendium's own cross-reference) rather than new teaching content. Not blocking: the slide is still fully followable without a fix -- "this could be tighter," not "I cannot follow this." The other bullets checked clean against all three classes: chunk 1's closing-summary bullet is maintainer-attested as deliberate and observation-grade (2026-08-07 accept-note), not a doctrine restatement; chunk 2's Goal drift / Plausible-but-wrong mechanism sentences are maintainer-attested deliberate doubling (Slide-size-guard note) that the rule's own §7 sibling-discipline explicitly protects, not empty repetition; chunk 3's test->learn->encode bullet maps each arc stage to a concrete referent rather than restating the header.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Cut the middle sentence and let the reflex description and its payoff carry the point: "...the reflex is to fix it immediately: edit the prompt, add a constraint, reach for the next tool. The failures earn the validation that catches them."
